title: Arrays and Algorithms Mastery Contract
purpose: Build defensible arrays-and-algorithms fluency through reconstruction, explanation, executable tests, and transfer rather than passive exposure.

claimDefense.rule: Repository code is study material, not proof of personal mastery. A problem becomes defensible only after a blank-file, no-AI reconstruction, correct explanation, harness pass, and transfer exercise.

sessionTemplate.activity: write or explain the baseline solution
record complexity, confusion, evidence, and next rep

twoSumMastery.contract: Given an integer sequence and target, return two distinct indices whose values sum to the target; this repository raises ValueError when no pair exists.
invariants: The current value needs a complement equal to target minus current value.
The seen map contains only values from earlier indices.
Check for the complement before inserting the current value so a value cannot reuse its own index and duplicate pairs such as [3, 3] still work.
graduationGates: State the input/output contract without looking it up.
Write the brute-force solution from memory and explain why the loops start at different indices.
Derive complement = target - value without copying a remembered solution.
Write the hash-map solution from a blank file without AI assistance.
Explain why lookup-before-insert handles [3, 3] and prevents reusing the same index.
Explain O(n^2)/O(1) versus average O(n)/O(n) tradeoffs.
Pass the executable harness after reconstruction.
Solve a transfer variant that uses the same lookup or two-pointer idea.

exercises.prompt: Given an array, narrate index, value, previous state, and next state for one complete linear scan without writing code first.
Write Two Sum with nested loops from a blank file and explain why right begins at left + 1.
Rewrite Two Sum using a complement hash map from a blank file, then explain lookup-before-insert.
Defend Two Sum against duplicates, negatives, zero, no solution, and self-reuse edge cases.
Detect whether an array contains a duplicate, first with a baseline comparison and then with a set.
Build a frequency map and use it to identify values occurring more than once.
Compute the best single buy/sell profit with one pass while explaining the running-minimum invariant.
Find a maximum-sum contiguous subarray and explain the restart-versus-extend decision.
Build prefix sums and answer several range-sum queries from the precomputed structure.
Produce product-of-array-except-self without division using prefix and suffix state.
Solve a sorted pair-sum problem with left/right pointers and state why each pointer movement is safe.
Reduce a three-value sum search to repeated two-pointer scans after sorting.
Find the maximum sum of any fixed-length window using enter/leave updates rather than recomputing each window.
Implement binary search twice: once with inclusive bounds and once with a half-open interval, then explain the loop invariants.
Take an unfamiliar array problem, write a correct baseline, classify the reusable pattern, optimize it, add edge tests, and defend complexity without AI assistance.

evidenceLedger.rule: Never mark defensible from an assisted-study attempt alone.

acceptanceContract.statement: The repository contains working brute-force and hash-map Two Sum reference implementations.
A dependency-free executable harness covers canonical, duplicate, negative, zero, self-reuse, no-solution, and input-mutation cases.
Two Sum mastery requires contract recall, blank-file no-AI reconstruction, lookup-before-insert explanation, complexity defense, and transfer.
The arrays roadmap advances from mechanics through hash lookup, running state, prefix/suffix, two pointers, windows, binary search, and an unfamiliar-problem capstone.
Each deliberate-practice session records executable evidence, confusion, next rep, and mastery state.
Committed reference code and AI-assisted work do not by themselves establish personal mastery or freelancer expertise.
